newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: CRICKET-CRONJE LEADS IRELAND TO HISTORIC VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRONJE LEADS IRELAND TO HISTORIC VICTORY.

text.p: Ireland's cricketers, led by South Africa captain Hansie Cronje, completed an historic victory in the Benson and Hedges Cup at Clontarf on Tuesday.
The Irish beat Middlesex by 46 runs, their first win over an English county side in the 50 overs competition which also includes Scotland, Minor Counties and British Universities.
Middlesex, facing Ireland's 281 for four, were in big trouble at 134 for six off 32.2 overs when rain ended play on Monday.
They succeeded only in reaching 235 all out from 46.4 overs after play resumed on Tuesday under threatening skies.
Ireland had not won a game since they entered the Cup in 1994.
Cronje, signed to lead Ireland for four matches in the group stage of the competition at the suggestion of South African cricket chief Ali Bacher, batted at number four and hit an unbeaten 94.
The South African also took two wickets, including that of Mark Ramprakash.
Ireland's previous most famous cricketing victory was in a one-day game at the expense of the touring West Indies in 1969.
